description: R7/TN5 spike: gpui-component's List, Input, Switch and Dialog each emit an AccessKit node carrying their visible text once the tree is activated (automation `a11y` verb), proving the pattern Phase 1's real views (U4) must follow
notes: The spike route (`Route::A11ySpike`) exists only in automation builds; `open_view` refuses it in any build without this feature because the route itself does not exist.
All four widgets reach the tree with their documented API, no workaround: see desktop-gpui/probes/A11Y-NOTES.md and the module doc on desktop-gpui/src/views/a11y_spike.rs.

List rows: the row's own text (a `text!` child, same rule Task 6 found for a bare title) is a separate Label node nested under the row container, which is the node List itself marks `role: ListItem` and `selected`. That is why the row's text and its selected flag are asserted as two separate `see` queries rather than one.

Dialog: opened through `window.open_dialog` on the spike view's first render, mounted by gpui-component's `WindowState` root plugin above the panel's own content — not a child of the div tree the other three widgets sit in.

Dialog's OWN container never carries `role: Dialog` in gpui-pre 0.3.7: gpui_base::Dialog's render calls `.focus_trap(...)`, whose FocusTrapContainer wrapper forwards `prepaint` straight to the inner div's raw Element method instead of through gpui-pre's Drawable wrapper, which is the only place an a11y node gets pushed (element.rs's `ElementDrawPhase::prepaint`). The inner div's `.role(Role::Dialog)` is consequently never seen. Its CHILDREN (the title, the Close button) are unaffected because Div::prepaint wraps each child in its own Drawable. The step below pins this as a known, asserted gap (not a silent omission) rather than requiring a node that cannot exist with this gpui-pre version — see A11Y-NOTES.md.

Task 11 (ruling on concern 5): the Input holds keyboard focus from the first frame (a11y_spike.rs). Escape closes the dialog (gpui-component's own binding) and hands focus back to it; the automation `key` verb's keystrokes then reach the Input as typed text through GPUI's own dispatch (Window::dispatch_keystroke -> the focused element's input handler), so the Input's a11y value changes; Backspace deletes. Tab is gpui-base Root's binding (focus_next) and moves focus to the Switch, whose a11y node then carries the focused flag (the dump's gpui_focus). link-browser-filter and onboarding depend on both.

Task 11 fix round 1: with the Input still focused, End/Home/Down/Up move the List's selection (the List's selected flag), because the view intercepts the Input's MoveEnd/MoveHome/MoveDown/MoveUp actions with capture_action on a parent and stops propagation. A focused single-line Input otherwise swallows those keys, and a parent's on_key_down never sees them, since GPUI dispatches a matched binding's action before raw key listeners. Typing still reaches the Input afterwards, so focus never left it. Phase 1's browser needs exactly this (A11Y-NOTES.md 'Keyboard').

List: all three rows carry role ListItem
List: each row's text! child is a Label, in row order
List: alpha (row 0) carries the selected flag List itself sets
List: beta and gamma are not selected
Input: role TextInput, value is the visible text
Switch: role Switch, label as its name, toggled true (on)
Dialog: its title is a Label, same text! pattern as everything else here (the dialog IS mounted and visible, confirmed by this reaching the tree at all)
Dialog: known gap, pinned so a future gpui-pre fixing it is noticed rather than silently still passing — see the notes above and A11Y-NOTES.md

a Button carries the focused flag (what onboarding/settings key_until rely on)

dialog gone

nothing focused in the tree but the Input yet

the Switch now carries the focused flag
Shift-Tab moves it back
the Switch is no longer focused
and typing reaches the Input again
